title: Hummus: A Dataset of Humorous Multimodal Metaphor Use

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent on decoding); max_tokens covers a Yes/No answer

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: test set (Table 6 'All' test = 286 items; test_set.json in the repository)

items.source: https://github.com/xiaoyuisrain/humorous-multimodal-metaphor-use: hummus_dataset.json (annotations), images/ (New Yorker cartoons from the CapCon corpus), test_set.json (test ids)
items.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (repository LICENSE); CapCon images CC-BY-4.0

fields_prose.label: met_class in {Yes, WIDLII, No} (positive = Yes or WIDLII)

items.columns_verified: hummus_dataset.json = dict keyed by item id (1,000 entries; the runner flattens it with id = key) with caption, contest_number, met_class (No 372, Yes 332, WIDLII 236, Discard 60); test_set.json is NOT at the repository root on main (404) - the 286 test ids still have to be located; images are not in the repository listing fetched

prompt.user_template:
{image}Caption: {caption}

Does the humor of the given image-and-caption combination involve metaphor use? Answer the question with Yes or No.

placeholders.image: attach images/<id>.jpg as an image content part (NOT expressible: the runner sends text only)
placeholders.caption: items.caption

prompt.source_location: Table 1 (Classification instruction) with the full-prompt layout in the Table 1 caption: <image> + 'Caption: {caption}\n\n{instructions}'

output.postprocess: strip; no match = unsuccessful answer (counted as wrong; success rate reported)
output.parse_prose: label from set [Yes, No]: first case-insensitive match

metric.name: macro_f1
metric.definition: mean of F1(positive class: gold Yes/WIDLII, prediction Yes) and F1(negative class: gold No, prediction No) over the 286 test items ('Classification Avg'). (= macro F1 over the two classes Yes/No after mapping WIDLII -> Yes; runner macro_f1)
metric.original_location: Table 2, row GPT-4 Turbo, Classification columns Pos 0.64 / Neg 0.47 / Avg 0.56
